source.title: Weak-to-Strong Honesty Alignment via Learning-to-Rank Supervision
source.authors: Yunfan Xie; Li-Xin Zou; Dan Luo; Min Tang; Chenliang Li

record.file_problem: No major problem; the full paper text is present. Some figures are flattened, and the main results table is flattened but its model, dataset, method, and metric layout supports assigning the reported values.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies weak-supervision fine-tuning to honesty alignment and reports behavioral outcomes, but its honest-head pseudo-labeling procedure and honesty metrics differ from Burns et al.'s original method and PGR measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports honesty-score results for WHAT Pair and WHAT List alongside SFT, and compares the two ranking-loss variants. It does not report the honest head's standalone performance as a weak supervisor, a strong-model true-label ceiling, or PGR. Thus the reported honesty comparisons do not directly establish that the fine-tuned student beats its weak supervisor or quantify a recovered gap. The paper also discusses honesty-ratio and hidden-layer sensitivity; the layer-choice results are figure-based and the honesty-ratio discussion does not test a listed version's specified comparison.
record.test_reason: Applies weak-to-strong fine-tuning to honesty alignment, a new setting. Figure 2 compares the student fine-tuned on pseudo-labels with the supervisor's own reranked outputs (Honest-aware Decoding). That is a student-versus-supervisor comparison. There is no true-label ceiling and no PGR. The 'weak' supervisor is an MLP head on the same LLM's hidden states, combined with that LLM's likelihood, so it is not a smaller model.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that WHAT (a learning-to-rank honest head that self-labels unannotated questions, followed by fine-tuning) achieves state-of-the-art honesty with scarce labels and preserves general ability. They note no theoretical analysis, only smaller models tested, and weaker over-conservativeness scores.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a 3-layer MLP honest head over an LLM's intermediate representations, trained with pairwise or listwise ranking, to rerank beam-search candidates and create pseudo-labels for LoRA fine-tuning. This differs from the original weak-to-strong setup and does not calculate Burns et al.'s PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: Honesty-head input layer is reported to affect performance; the paper says layer choice matters. The honesty ratio β also affects outcomes: β=1 substantially raises over-conservativeness and lowers honesty, while β=0 gives only minor improvements. The paper says the listwise-versus-pairwise result differs in two of nine model-dataset settings.

fits_no_version.finding: WHAT (head-reranked self-labels plus fine-tuning) beats gold-label SFT and DPO on honesty score in all 9 model-dataset settings. The listwise head beats the pairwise head in 7 of 9.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Self-labeling with a reranking head trained on scarce labels improves honesty over SFT on those labels alone.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 2025
record.problems: The paper does not report a standalone weak-supervisor score, a true-label strong-model ceiling, or PGR, so its principal comparisons cannot answer the student-versus-supervisor or gap-recovery question. The authors also state that the empirical analysis lacks theoretical underpinnings and that experiments are restricted to smaller models.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted due to the 60-row limit. The paper's separate accuracy, harmlessness, and general-ability comparisons are not included because the extracted rows focus on the reported Honesty Score results relevant to the claim.

untested.parts: No strong-model ceiling and no PGR. The supervisor is not a smaller or weaker model.
No auxiliary confidence loss, no supervisor ensembling measured by PGR, and no naive weak-to-strong baseline. Pair versus List changes only the supervisor's loss.
No PGR across sizes or tasks, and no analysis of what predicts PGR.

missing.what: Honesty score of Honest-aware Decoding (the supervisor's labels) versus the WHAT student: Llama 70.83/72.49, 61.31/62.34, 61.72/62.89; second panel 76.47/78.31, 63.89/65.02, 62.01/63.81. Panel titled Gemma, but its values match Mistral in Table 1.
Honesty ratio β sensitivity. β=0 (best-of-N) gives minor gains; β=1 (head only) raises over-conservativeness and lowers honesty. Figure only, no numbers.

record.verdict_notes: Whether this is weak-to-strong in Burns et al.'s sense is doubtful. Supervisor and student share the same LLM, so it is closer to self-training with a reranker. The V1 support is therefore weak evidence. Figure 2 panel labelling is inconsistent: the title says Gemma, the legend and values say Mistral.

versions.untested_parts: No standalone weak-supervisor score, true-label strong-model ceiling, or PGR is reported, so the student-versus-supervisor comparison and gap recovery cannot be determined.
The study compares pairwise and listwise honest-head losses using honesty scores, but does not measure PGR or isolate auxiliary confidence loss or supervisor ensembling.

Reports honesty scores across three models and three datasets, but not PGR; no systematic model-size sweep, chess task, reward modelling, or predictor analysis is reported. Hidden-layer sensitivity is shown in a figure.
Does not test supervisor-uncheckable behavior, distribution shift, or shared student-supervisor errors.
No theoretical conditions for a student to beat its supervisor are tested or derived.
No vision or other non-language modality is tested.

relationships.condition: Llama and a second model (Mistral by its values) on PopQA, SQuAD and Non-AmbigQA, honesty score
relationships.reason: Per Figure 2 (no rows), the fine-tuned student beats Honest-aware Decoding in all 6 settings. Gains are about 1-2 points, e.g. Llama PopQA 72.49 vs 70.83. There is no ceiling, and the supervisor is not a smaller model.
relationships.display_finding: Students gained approximately 1–2 honesty points across all six settings, including 72.49 versus 70.83 for Llama on PopQA, although supervision did not come from a smaller model.

source_check.condition: Llama and a second model (Mistral by its values) on PopQA, SQuAD and Non-AmbigQA, honesty score
source_check.reason: Figure 2 shows WHAT above Honest-aware Decoding in all six comparisons: Llama 72.49>70.83, 62.34>61.31, 62.89>61.72; second model 78.31>76.47, 65.02>63.89, 63.81>62.01. The second model's values match Mistral in Table 1, although the extracted figure labels include Gemma. These comparisons support positive gains in this setting; PGR and a strong ceiling are unreported.

labels.reason: Figure 2 shows WHAT above Honest-aware Decoding in all six comparisons: Llama 72.49>70.83, 62.34>61.31, 62.89>61.72; second model 78.31>76.47, 65.02>63.89, 63.81>62.01. These comparisons support positive gains in this setting; PGR and a strong ceiling are unreported.

relation.reason: The ablation measures whether fine-tuning on weak-head-guided pseudo-labels improves performance beyond Honest-aware Decoding.

tranche.reason: Honesty alignment is a new setting, and Figure 2 compares the pseudo-label-trained student against the decoding pipeline that supplies its supervision.

source_check.notes: Table 1 comparisons cannot establish student-over-supervisor gains; the supporting comparisons are in Figure 2 and are missing from the listed rows. Figure 2's second-model labeling is inconsistent with its Mistral-matching values; the supervisor uses the target LLM plus a small honest head.

statements.correction: Sections 3.1–3.3: weak supervisor = 3-layer MLP honest head using the target LLM's intermediate representations; pseudo-labels combine head scores with LLM likelihoods. Figure 2: Llama PopQA WHAT 72.49; Honest-aware Decoding 70.83. No separate smaller generative LLM.
statements.problem: The gains are correct, but saying the supervisor is not a smaller model conflates the full Honest-aware Decoding pipeline with its explicitly lightweight honest-head component.
